This is a super interesting game that will hook you for a few evenings—perhaps a few weeks, but not much longer. It’s rewarding to develop and create your own laboratories, interacting with the world. But at some point it becomes too easy: once you have a couple of labs, you quickly start farming dealers, and the game loses its angle due to the sheer abundance.
I know the developer does it all by himself, and I have a lot of respect for that. Yet it seems that introducing new cities as you level up and expand your territory would significantly boost the interest.
It’s worth noting how fun the game is. Overall, the map could use a bit more space: after a couple of gaming sessions you know every corner and feel like there’s nowhere left to grow.
My take: adding a couple more cities you can relocate to after gaining full control over the previous ones would restore the hype and give the game a fresh breath of air.

Schedule I is the kind of game that makes you question your life choices, mostly because you’re suddenly very invested in running a criminal empire with the organizational skills of a sleep-deprived raccoon.

You start small, just trying to survive, and before you know it you’re micromanaging production, dodging the law, and thinking, “Wow, I’m actually not that bad at crime.” The game does an excellent job of making you feel powerful and extremely paranoid at the same time.

The mechanics are surprisingly deep, which is funny considering your character’s career path. There’s strategy, risk management, and enough chaos to keep you constantly on edge.

Graphics are simple but effective and the gameplay loop is addicting in a “just one more run before I ruin everything” kind of way. Schedule I doesn’t glorify crime, it just proves that running an illegal operation is hard, exhausting, and probably not worth it… but wow, is it fun.

Final verdict:
10/10 stress, 0/10 life advice

Schedule 1 is one of those games you pick up when you want to dive into a life of crime and chaos. It really captures the thrill of living like a cartel lord or feeling like you're in the Breaking Bad TV show sitting on piles of cash, hanging out with your crew, dodging cops, and delivering your goods. The game makes you feel like you're breaking the rules, doing things you probably shouldn’t, like mixing gasoline into your concoctions and hoping the customers don’t notice.

It brings back memories of classic gangster games, similar to the earlier Saints Row titles, where you truly felt like part of a gang. The gameplay is satisfying and immersive, especially in co-op mode, where playing with friends creates memorable moments that you find yourself sharing in real life, sometimes making people question what you were up to the night before.

Overall, I give Schedule 1 a 10 out of 10. It’s fun, engaging, and the cooperative play amplifies the chaos and enjoyment. Whether you're managing your empire or just goofing around with friends, it’s a game that delivers a unique blend of strategy, humor, and crime sandbox action.
